rationale: Ordinary native KS requests up to 32 independent original XC tiles within an additional allowance of 32 MiB times the larger AO/density-product jet count (32 MiB when both are one, 128 MiB when either is four). GGA AO panels therefore retain capacity even with one density-product jet. Explicit byte caps are exact, and automatic allocation rejection retries the original 32-MiB allowance. Compiler residency admission and the shared numeric resource ledger retain one-tile execution on tiny/response/mixed/resource-rejected domains; explicit zero/one tile or zero-byte overrides retain the incumbent. Independent E/V and complete cold/warm/moved E/F gates qualify the policy without added per-build AO/jet/contraction work. Point algebra and ordered accumulation are unchanged.
revisit_condition: Refine resource/profitability admission using additional devices and workloads, not device or molecule-size whitelists. Retain opt-out, constrained-memory fallback and ordered E/V semantics. The small cold population, differing cold trajectories, hardware-counter permissions and separate #2072 composition remain disclosed follow-up qualification, not claims of universal profitability.
